_what_this_is: CARRIED ITEMS AND STANDING RULINGS THAT BELONG TO NO ONE FORM'S MAP. Every map carries its own `_carried` list and every form's gate reports that list's length, which works exactly as long as the item belongs to a form that HAS a map. A ruling made about 433-D before 433-D has a map has nowhere to live, and a ruling with nowhere to live is a ruling that evaporates - which is the failure this construct exists to prevent, one level up from the per-map lists.
_the_rule: Unresolved is fine. Evaporating is not. An item leaves this file in exactly two ways: it is RESOLVED, with what resolved it, or it is WITHDRAWN, with why it was not a question after all.
_how_an_item_leaves_for_a_map: When the form it names gets a map, the item is COPIED into that map's `_carried.open` in the first commit of that form's track and marked `migrated_to` here. It is not deleted: a cross-form ruling that shaped a form's first prompt should still be readable from outside that form.
_authored: Prompt 36, the 433-A(OIC) naming and provisioning pass.

open.subject: 433-D's duplicate pages need a declared `mirror`, and a mirror is a declaration and not an exemption
open.the_shape: Page 3 of 433-D is the taxpayer's copy of page 1. Every leaf stem appears exactly TWICE across the two pages, and the same value must reach both copies.
open.why_it_is_a_problem_today: That is INTENTIONAL double-binding, and the duplicate-write guard has correctly forbidden double-binding since Prompt 4. A map that binds one key to two targets is the exact shape of the defect that guard exists to catch, so 433-D cannot be mapped under the current rules without either breaking the guard or declaring the mirror.
open.the_ruling: Declare it. A `mirror` block names the mirrored pairs, and the declaration is CHECKED: every stem in a mirrored pair appears exactly twice, both copies receive the same value, and a stem bound to only one copy is a STOP. An exemption would be a hiding place - it would let any second binding through under the word 'mirror'. A checked declaration is not.
open.built_when: 433-D's FIRST prompt, not before. Recorded here so the ruling survives the seven or more prompts between the two OIC forms and 433-D.
open.status: OPEN - recorded, not built. No 433-D map exists.

open.subject: 433-H is out of this engine's scope, and the revision pin cannot mean there what it means everywhere else
open.the_shape: 433-H is XFA-only and dynamic: ZERO AcroForm fields, one static page carrying the Adobe Reader placeholder. Nothing this engine does - enumerate fields, correlate labels by rectangle, fill, read back - has an input.
open.the_sharper_half: Its revision and catalog number came from the INFLATED XFA PACKET and not from drawn page bytes. Every other form in this repo pins its revision against text drawn on the page, and confirm-form-revision-from-page-bytes is a standing rule. A pin read from an XFA packet is not evidence of the same kind, and treating the two as interchangeable would quietly weaken the rule for every form.
open.the_ruling: Do not attempt it, and do not fold it into any prompt for the other forms. It becomes a SEPARATE FEASIBILITY TRACK after 433-A(OIC), 433-B(OIC), 433-B and 433-D, and the first question that track must answer is whether we fill an XFA form at all or author a static replica.
open.status: OPEN - scope change recorded rather than absorbed.

open.subject: 433-B(OIC) is next, and the reason is inheritance rather than size
open.the_shape: 86 of 433-B(OIC)'s 178 distinct leaf names are shared with 433-A(OIC) and 1 with 433-A. 433-B shares 11 with 433-A and ZERO with 433-A(OIC).
open.the_ruling: 433-B(OIC) is next, not 433-B. The registry, the row-class assertion and the trap list inherit down the OIC line and essentially not across it, so 433-B(OIC) banks that inheritance while it is warm, at 267 fields against 447. The OIC pair is also the useful pair: an individual OIC and a business OIC together are a FILING, where 433-B alone is not.
open.what_it_inherits_that_must_be_re_checked: The safe-deposit suffix inversion [L21] is present on 433-A too, so it is inherited from the shared source rather than being an OIC quirk - and 433-B and 433-B(OIC) must be READ for it before their safe-deposit rows are bound, not assumed to have it or to lack it.
open.status: OPEN - sequencing ruling, acted on when 433-A(OIC) closes.

open.the_ruling: Each remaining form's blank PDF goes into adapters/pdf/forms/ in the FIRST COMMIT of that form's track, with its SHA-256 recorded, so the revision pin has an artefact to pin against instead of a download that may not be the same file next week.

resolved.subject: eight 433-A groups declare no row_class, so eight printed tables route rows by group name alone
resolved.the_shape: adapters/hubspot/asset-row-shapes.json declares that 433-A prints digital assets (15a-15d), life insurance (17a-17e), personal assets (20a/20b), business assets (67a/67b), accounts and notes receivable (66a-66e), credit cards accepted (63a/63b/63c), payment processors (62a/62b) and the Section 1 household members table. adapters/pdf/maps/433a.map.json binds all eight, and not one of those groups declares a `row_class`. Six 433-A groups do declare one.
resolved.why_it_is_a_problem_today: check-row-shape.mjs skips every group without a row_class - `if (!rc || !Array.isArray(rc.accepts)) continue;` - so nothing asserts that a row landing in one of those eight tables is a row of that class. That is defect D1 exactly: a row filed under the wrong group prints under a printed heading it does not belong under, on a statement signed under penalty of perjury, and every printed total still reconciles. The row_class construct exists to make that inexpressible and it was never extended to these eight.
resolved.what_was_done: DECLARED, not fixed. Each of the eight now carries an `unrouted` block in asset-row-shapes.json naming the 433-A group, the printed table and this consequence, and adapters/pdf/assert-row-shape-spec.mjs [A3] reports all eight on every run and STOPS if one loses its declaration or if a declaration goes stale because the gap closed.
resolved.why_it_is_not_resolved_here: Giving those groups a `row_class` is a routing change to the fill engine for a filed form, on a form whose track this prompt is not on. It also needs a per-group decision this audit is not the place to take: `personal_property` on 433-A is the very binding C-22 turned on, and adding a class to `property_line_20` would settle part of that question by side effect rather than on its evidence.
resolved.built_when: 433-A's next track, before any further 433-A crosswalk work. It is cheap - eight `row_class` blocks and no printed cell moves - and check-row-shape.mjs reports rather than fails a row that states no class, so it cannot break a passing gate.
resolved.what_resolved_it: TWELVE row_class declarations, not the eight this item was filed for. The item named 433-A's eight; enumerating every group on every mapped form gives twelve - 433-A 8, 433-F 3, 433-A(OIC) 1 - and all twelve are declared. Each class is settled from the PRINTED PAGE, with the heading text and its drawn coordinates quoted in the group's row_class._why, and each is proved to route by adapters/pdf/assert-row-class-routes.mjs, which poisons every declaring group with a class it does not accept and requires the fill engine to STOP and name the row. 64 poisoned runs across 32 declaring groups, 64 refusals.
resolved.the_set_was_derived_rather_than_taken: THE ITEM'S OWN FIGURE WAS RIGHT FOR THE FORM IT NAMED AND WRONG FOR THE REPO. Eight was correct for 433-A. The defect - a group routing rows by group name alone - stood in twelve places, and the four beyond 433-A sat on two other FINISHED forms. Fixing the filed eight and reporting D-05 closed would have left the original defect standing on a form JLW has filled and tested, under a commit message saying it was fixed.
resolved.and_the_instrument_had_been_switched_off: The three on 433-F were invisible to adapters/pdf/assert-row-shape-spec.mjs [A3], which is the check written to find exactly this. asset-row-shapes.json declared 433-F's DIGITAL ASSETS, E1 and E2 tables "printed, not currently mapped"; claimsNothing() excuses that phrase from the routing assertion; and 433f.map.json has bound all three since they were authored, each group's own _why saying in terms that the shared row class binds. A stale sentence in the spec turned the assertion off over three tables, and excusedClaims() printed all three on every run with nothing comparing them to the map. Claims corrected in the same commit; excused claims fall from 7 to 4 and declared routing gaps from 8 to 0.
resolved.no_row_moved: PROVED, NOT ASSERTED. Every 433-A group was snapshotted cell by cell from the filled PDF before and after - 290 cells across 14 groups, same target and same printed value in every one. verify-headings reports 0 findings on all three forms both sides. A row_class declares what a row must SAY it is; it moves no cell.
resolved.what_it_cost: Twelve row_class blocks, eight retired unrouted declarations, three corrected printed-table claims, asset_class on 82 fixture rows, and one derived-scope routing assertion. No printed cell moved on any form.
